raw_case_text:
A 53-year-old morbidly obese female with a history of hypertension presented to the emergency department (ED), with a sudden onset of loss of consciousness, left-sided weakness, and altered sensorium for two days, which was associated with high-grade fever and vomiting. At admission, she was unconscious (Glasgow coma scale, or GCS, score = 5); had tachypnea (respiratory rate, or RR, 30-35 minute-1), tachycardia (heart rate, or HR, 114 bpm), and blood pressure (BP) 153/90 mmHg; was maintaining oxygen saturation of 94% to 94% (on room air) on spontaneous respiration; and was passing urine output around 40-50 mL/hour. Given airway protection, tracheal intubation was performed immediately. Post intubation, the GCS was 6. Noncontrast computerized tomography (NCCT) of the brain revealed right basal ganglia bleeding with intraventricular hemorrhage (Figure 1).
Then she was transferred to ICU, where cerebral protection strategy (head-up position, neck in a neutral position, osmotic diuretics, mean arterial pressure (MAP) 85-90 mm Hg, normoxia, normocarbia, euglycemia, normothermia, and maintenance of sodium (Na+) levels between 145 and 155 mEq/L) and further supportive care was initiated. Laboratory evaluation at admission is summarized in Table 1. Electrocardiography (ECG) showed sinus tachycardia. Chest X-ray (CXR) was normal.   
After a few days of ICU admission, she started spiking high-grade temperature (core temperature as high as 106-107  F), which was associated with rhabdomyolysis (serum creatine kinase (CK-total) = 10,000 IU/L), stage III acute kidney injury (AKI, requiring five sessions of renal replacement therapy), and coagulopathy (requiring blood component therapy). On workup, cultures turned out to be sterile. Other possibilities of hyperthermia (such as drug toxicity) were ruled out. NCCT head was repeated, which did not reveal any hematoma expansion. Workup for COVID-19 was also negative. On account of a history of fever with chill and myalgia around a week before ED admission, a tropical workup was sent for malaria, typhoid, leptospirosis, dengue, chikungunya, and scrub typhus, in which serology (IgM antibodies) for dengue turned out to be positive. Gradually, the temperature trends, renal functions, and coagulopathy recovered. In intercurrent issues, she had septic shock (secondary to ventilator-associated pneumonia and grade IV pressure injury in the sacral region) and neuromuscular weakness, resulting in prolonged weaning. Eventually, the patient was discharged after six months of ICU stay in tracheostomized condition, with a GCS score of 9, accepting Ryle's tube feeding and passing adequate urine output.

subjective.chief_complaint: A 53-year-old morbidly obese, hypertensive female presented unconscious with a 2-day history of sudden loss of consciousness, left-sided weakness, high-grade fever, and vomiting, preceded 1 week earlier by fever with chills and myalgia.
subjective.history_of_present_illness: One week after experiencing fever with chills and myalgia, the patient developed high-grade fever, vomiting, acute left-sided weakness, and coma for 2 days prior to ED presentation. During her ICU stay for a right basal ganglia intracerebral hemorrhage, she developed extreme hyperpyrexia (106-107 F), severe rhabdomyolysis, stage III acute kidney injury requiring dialysis, and coagulopathy.
subjective.past_medical_history: Morbid obesity and hypertension; febrile prodrome with chills and myalgia 1 week prior to admission.
subjective.review_of_systems: Positive for prodromal fever, chills, and myalgia, followed by high-grade fever (spiking to 106-107 F in ICU), vomiting, left-sided hemiparesis, and coma.

objective.physical_examination: On admission: unconscious with GCS 5/15 (6/15 post-intubation), tachypneic (RR 30-35/min), tachycardic (HR 114 bpm), blood pressure 153/90 mmHg, room-air SpO2 94%, left-sided weakness, and urine output 40-50 mL/h. In the ICU: extreme core hyperthermia (106-107 F), later complicated by a grade IV sacral pressure injury and ICU neuromuscular weakness.
objective.routine_investigations: Admission ECG showed sinus tachycardia and CXR was normal. In the ICU, she developed severe rhabdomyolysis (serum total CK 10,000 IU/L), stage III AKI, and coagulopathy; blood/body fluid cultures, COVID-19 testing, and tropical fever tests for malaria, typhoid, leptospirosis, chikungunya, and scrub typhus were all negative.
objective.advanced_workup: Admission non-contrast head CT revealed a right basal ganglia intracerebral hemorrhage with intraventricular extension (repeat head CT showed no hematoma expansion).

assessment_and_plan.assessment_and_confirmation: Acute dengue fever complicated by right basal ganglia intracerebral and intraventricular hemorrhage, extreme central/infectious hyperpyrexia (106-107 F), rhabdomyolysis (CK 10,000 IU/L), coagulopathy, and stage III acute kidney injury, confirmed by positive dengue IgM serology and head CT. Managed in the ICU with neuroprotective mechanical ventilation, osmotic diuretics, 5 sessions of renal replacement therapy, blood component transfusions, and treatment for secondary ventilator-associated pneumonia and sacral pressure ulcer; discharged after 6 months tracheostomized with GCS 9, normal renal function, and nasogastric feeding.
